agency: New York City Department of Correction
outcome_detail: The mass litigation remains active as of 2026. More than 700 Adult Survivors Act suits (719 per CBS New York) seek over $14 billion collectively; no comprehensive settlement has been announced. The city has settled a small number of individual cases (e.g., $1.6 million in May 2024 to a detainee abused by a Rikers physical therapist, and other individual settlements reported at $1.2 million and $500,000). In November 2025 the City Council reopened the Gender-Motivated Violence Act lookback window for 18 months, enabling further suits, and new suits were still being filed as of December 2025.
criminal_detail: In April 2024 the Bronx District Attorney assembled a team of prosecutors to review Rikers sexual-assault claims, but as of late 2024 no criminal charges connected to the lawsuits had been announced, and Gothamist reported that several guards named in pending suits remained employed at Rikers. Separate individual prosecutions exist: Rikers physical therapist Carlos Negron pleaded guilty in February 2022 to a felony criminal sexual act count, and correction officer Kelvin Williams was indicted in 2024 by the Bronx DA for sexual assault of a Rikers inmate.
incident_date_approx: Alleged abuse spanning decades, from at least the 1980s through the 2020s, largely at the Rose M. Singer Center women's jail
description: More than 700 lawsuits filed against New York City under the state's Adult Survivors Act — which opened a one-year window (November 2022 to November 2023) for sexual-assault claims outside the statute of limitations — allege that Department of Correction officers and staff sexually assaulted people held at Rikers Island over several decades, mostly women detained at the Rose M. Singer Center. According to the complaints, officers assaulted detainees during invasive searches and at night, and coerced sexual acts with offers of phone access and contraband; the suits collectively seek more than $14 billion. A Gothamist analysis found that nearly 60% of the 1,256 ASA suits filed in New York City's supreme courts described assaults at Rikers. The litigation is ongoing: the city has settled only a handful of individual cases, the Bronx DA opened a review of the claims, and additional suits continued to be filed into 2025-2026, including under the city's reopened Gender-Motivated Violence Act window.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (corrections).
